summary: The Italian military said Friday that the navy had recaptured the fishing boat Airone hours after armed men seized it off Sicily. Naval personnel boarded the vessel about 90 kilometers (56 miles) from Libya's port of Misrata and detained a Libyan soldier, according to military statements. The navy said accidental rifle fire during the operation slightly injured one of the seven fishermen aboard. The crew, comprising three Sicilians and four Tunisians, had left Mazara del Vallo five days earlier to catch shrimp.

Novak Djokovic extended his current winning streak to 17 matches after beating Thomas Berdych 7-5, 4-6, 6-3 in the rain-interrupted final of the Monte Carlo Masters. "It was a tough match, a particular match," said Djokovic after winning his 52nd career title, and his second Monte Carlo Masters championship. After winning the Australian Open back in January, Djokovic has followed up with Masters' victories at Indian Wells and Miami. Sunday's victory over Berdych means he becomes the first man to win the opening three Masters tournaments of the season.

Police said former Satyam Computers Services chairman Ramalinga Raju and nine others received seven-year prison sentences after convictions for cheating, criminal conspiracy, breach of public trust and other offenses. A Central Bureau of Investigation spokesman said Raju was also fined $804,000. The case involved $1.6 billion in fraud exposed in 2009 when Raju acknowledged overstating profits through invented assets and cash, although investigators said investors' losses were considerably larger. Following the disclosures, India's government dismissed Satyam's board, and Tech Mahindra acquired the company through a state-backed auction.

Photographer Johan Bavman documents fathers taking full advantage of Sweden's parental leave, looking for a total of 60 fathers for an exhibition and a book; so far he's found 35. Sweden grants 480 calendar days of shared parental leave, with 390 paid at 80% of income up to 3,160 euros a month and 60 reserved as "daddy months" that are lost if unused, but only 12% of Swedish couples equally share the leave, Bavman said.

Officials said ISIS freed more than 200 Yazidis on Wednesday, with Kurdish government official Nuri Osman reporting 217 releases and Peshmerga commander Rassol Omar putting the number at 228. The freed captives, mostly women and children with the remainder elderly or ill, were taken by Kurdish forces to Irbil; the reason for their release remained unclear.

Philadelphia police added an attempted-murder charge against Nyia Parler, 41, whom they accuse of leaving her 21-year-old son, a quadriplegic with cerebral palsy, in woods for more than four days while visiting her boyfriend in Maryland. Her son was hospitalized with dehydration, malnutrition and other injuries, while Maryland police said her extradition must await completion of unspecified treatment.

New research released by the Anne Frank House concludes that Anne and her older sister, Margot Frank, probably did not survive to March 1945, at least a month earlier than Anne's supposed death on March 31, 1945. Witnesses said both sisters had typhus symptoms before February 7, and most deaths caused by typhus occur around twelve days after the first symptoms appear, the researchers wrote; the exact dates of death remain unclear.

It's obvious that Tom Brady's love for his wife, model Gisele Bundchen, will never go out of fashion. Bundchen walked the runway for the last time Wednesday, and the New England Patriots quarterback wasn't just there to support her in person, he expressed his emotions to the world on Facebook.

French police said investigators had recovered the principal evidence from the Germanwings Flight 9525 crash site and were not expected to return. The aircraft crashed in the Alps on March 24, about 6 miles (10 kilometers) from Seyne-les-Alpes, killing all 150 aboard. Recovery workers found the flight data recorder on Thursday, after the cockpit voice recorder had been recovered in the days following the crash. Prosecutor Brice Robin said laboratories had distinguished 150 DNA profiles from more than 2,000 samples and that 470 personal belongings had been recovered, including 40 badly damaged phones unlikely to yield useful information. A private security company would guard the site until the remaining wreckage could be moved to secure locations for any further examination. Authorities accused co-pilot Andreas Lubitz of locking the captain out and deliberately crashing the aircraft, and France's BEA said preliminary recorder analysis indicated that he intentionally accelerated its descent. Lubitz had previously experienced depression and had withheld recent medical notes declaring him unfit to work from his employer.

With his early leap into the 2016 race, Marco Rubio is positioning himself as the next generation of GOP leadership. The Republican senator from Florida has announced that he is seeking the Republican presidential nomination, running on an optimistic message that he embodies the promise of the American Dream. Yet Rubio has been his own worst enemy on what could have been his two signature issues: immigration reform and Cuba relations. Back in 2013, Rubio was a member of the Senate "Gang of 8" that crafted a bipartisan proposal for comprehensive reform, including a path to citizenship for the nation's estimated 11 million undocumented immigrants. He later distanced himself from the bill after it ran into resistance from House Republicans, and now says he favors a piecemeal approach, starting with securing the border. No wonder the research firm Latino Decisions reports that, "We find no evidence that Rubio's candidacy will draw significant Latino support for his candidacy or for his party more generally." By clinging to the notion that isolating Cuba is better than engaging with the communist country, Rubio has marginalized himself on an issue where he could have provided insight and leadership. He is a fierce opponent of "Obamacare" and wants the law repealed. However, the Affordable Care Act has led to a 12.3% drop in the Hispanic uninsured rate, making Latinos the demographic with the largest gain in insurance, thanks to the law. Another Rubio weakness is his lack of bold policy proposals. Unfortunately, a fresh face on stale ideas is not a winning combination -- not for Rubio, and not for Latino voters.

At 42, Sudan is elderly in rhino years. He's the last known male northern white rhino left in the entire world. A total of five remain in captivity worldwide: three in Kenya, and one each at zoos in San Diego and the Czech Republic. In a race against time, international experts are resorting to science to try to sustain the subspecies.

President Obama and his Cuban counterpart, Raul Castro, greeted each other and shook hands Friday night at a dinner in Panama City for the Summit of the Americas. The two nations have barely been on speaking terms officially for more than 50 years, and the leaders' summit interactions represent the highest-level talks since a meeting between then-Vice President Richard Nixon and then-Prime Minister Fidel Castro in 1959. Obama announced in December he was seeking to engage Havana in talks over reopening embassies and removing barriers to commerce and travel, and discussed normalizing relations with Castro by phone Wednesday, according to Deputy National Security Adviser Ben Rhodes. Obama is expected to announce Cuba's removal from the United States' list of countries that sponsor terrorism, but a panel of experts was reviewing the State Department's report before he makes a final determination.

Jamal al-Labani had hoped to bring his pregnant wife and 2-year-daughter back to the United States from war-torn Yemen, but family members identified him as a victim killed in a mortar strike last week in Aden. Early Tuesday evening, the 45-year-old was on his way back from mosque prayers when he was hit in the back by shrapnel from a mortar shell and died minutes later, his family said. He is believed to be the first U.S. citizen killed in the current violence in Yemen. For the past three weeks, al-Labani had told family members he was concerned about not being able to evacuate, according to his cousin; two days before he was killed, he told his family the last option was to cross the border into Oman and fly to Egypt. More than 200 people have been killed in Aden in the past 11 days, according to Naef Al Bakri, Aden's deputy governor. The Council on American-Islamic Relations said Yemeni-Americans trapped in the conflict haven't gotten enough help from the U.S. government, while the State Department said there are no current plans to evacuate private U.S. citizens from Yemen. The State Department encouraged citizens to shelter in a secure location until able to depart safely and use commercial transportation options when available. As Saudi Arabia and other Arab nations target the rebels with airstrikes, some 16 million Yemenis living in provinces under Houthi control remained without power after a blackout that began Saturday night. The International Committee of the Red Cross said Sunday that Saudi Arabia has signed off on the delivery of medical supplies and personnel to Yemen.

Law enforcement officials said Saturday that the FBI was examining a potential terrorist threat in the United States that might have been inspired by ISIS. Intercepted communications and other intelligence prompted the inquiry, but no arrests had occurred and investigators did not know whether it reflected a real plan or merely an aspiration. Its precise nature was unavailable, although an official said parts of California were a focus and had increased security. The TSA notified police responsible for security outside airports, while officials cautioned that the possible threat was not necessarily connected to aviation. Other American cities also strengthened security as a precaution. A Homeland Security spokesman declined to discuss the specific case but described measures introduced over recent months, including extra checks at selected overseas airports, more random passenger and baggage searches on incoming flights, and additional screening through the travel authorization system. He also cited a more visible police presence at federal facilities beginning in February and outreach to local authorities and community leaders to counter violent extremism.

Lewis Hamilton took victory for the Silver Arrows at the Chinese Grand Prix -- only for his teammate Nico Rosberg to later claim he had ruined his race by driving slowly. The reigning world champion captured his 35th grand prix win with a peerless pole-to-flag win under Shanghai's sunny skies. Rosberg came home second for Mercedes, with Ferrari's Sebastian Vettel finishing third to collect his third straight podium of 2015 and Kimi Raikkonen fourth. Vettel is just 13 points behind Hamilton in the world championship and four points ahead of Rosberg, after the first three races of the year. Rosberg complained after the race that Hamilton's lackadaisical Sunday driving was holding him up, pushing him back into Vettel's thrall and taking life out of his tyres. Hamilton said it was his job to bring the car home and that he didn't do anything intentionally to slow the cars down. Hamilton has won two grands prix in 2015 while Rosberg has yet to climb onto the top step of the podium. Rosberg has the chance to exorcise his frustrations on track at the Bahrain Grand Prix in just seven day's time. Former Ferrari race winner Fernando Alonso finished his first race for the McLaren Honda partnership with 12th place in China, after missing the Australian Grand Prix because of a head injury sustained in testing and retiring in Malaysia.

Universal's "Furious 7" continues to build momentum at the Friday box office for a weekend debut in the $135 million-$138 million range, the largest opening in North America since fall 2013. The final film featuring the late Paul Walker, "Furious 7" is opening around the globe this weekend and earned a record-breaking $60 million internationally on Wednesday and Thursday for a possible worldwide debut approaching or crossing $300 million by the end of Easter Sunday.

Delaware father Steve Esmond is in stable condition and improving as his two boys remain in critical condition after they became sick -- perhaps from pesticide exposure, federal officials say -- during a trip to the U.S. Virgin Islands. The teens' mother, Theresa Devine, was treated at a hospital and released, and is in occupational therapy, the family's attorney, James Maron, said. EPA spokesman Elias Rodriguez said preliminary test results showed the presence of methyl bromide in the unit where the family was staying; the pesticide is not allowed to be used indoors. The EPA is investigating whether the family was made ill after a fumigation at the resort on March 18 and whether environmental regulations or laws were violated, and the U.S. Department of Justice has initiated a criminal investigation.

While the fight against ISIS in Syria and Iraq holds the world's gaze, a simultaneous transformation is getting less attention: the deterioration of al Qaeda. In an audio message released Sunday, al Qaeda confirmed that two of its leaders, known as Ustad Ahmad Farooq and Qari Abdullah Mansur, were killed in CIA drone strikes in January in North Waziristan, near the Afghan-Pakistan border. Florida-raised Adnan Shukrijumah, 39, who was in charge of al Qaeda's operations to attack the West, was killed in December in a Pakistani military operation. Texas-born Mohanad Mahmoud Al Farekh, who also played a planning role for al Qaeda's operations, was arrested in Pakistan last year. Indeed, al Qaeda has virtually no capacity to carry out attacks in the West. The last successful al Qaeda attack in the West was the London transportation system bombings a decade ago. To be sure, al Qaeda's Yemen-based affiliate, al Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula, or AQAP, continues to pose a threat to American aviation. The group has built hard-to-detect bombs, which it has placed on U.S.-bound flights. Luckily, those bombs were faulty or were detected. The group also trained one of the gunmen who attacked the offices of the satirical magazine Charlie Hebdo in Paris in January, killing 12, but it's not clear if AQAP had any direct role in planning this attack. Meanwhile, ISIS continues to attract Western recruits and also inspire "homegrown" terrorists in the West, but the core al Qaeda organization that killed almost 3,000 men, women and children on 9/11 is on life support.
